## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

arguments.newText:
## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.

## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra

takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report

  factories: the migration is the `wire:` FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key** —
  documented now (README env-preconfig section,
  docs/agents/providers.md §Translating proxies, `--help`) with its
  caveat: the override engages only when the declared wire DIFFERS from

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

## Unreleased

- fix(bindings): gh-1624 — the gh-1570 binding preflight no longer kills
  translating-proxy factories. `_validateModelEndpoint`'s vendor-prefix
  verdict was fatal on ANY endpoint, so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` +
  bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exit-64'd every boot on
  1.0.576 (the prefix is a routing key on a translating proxy, not a
  dialect declaration). The vendor-prefix check is now scoped to KNOWN
  catalog endpoints — mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown
  endpoints pass" rule: real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
  api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast, unknown/private
  endpoints carry the mismatch as a `ProviderModelBinding.warnings`
  entry rendered by the boot notice (`warning: binding — …`), never
  exit 64. **Breaking-change note for 1.0.576 upgraders behind proxy
  factories: the migration is the `wire:` FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key** —
  documented now (README env-preconfig section,
  docs/agents/providers.md §Translating proxies, `--help`) with its
  caveat: the override engages only when the declared wire DIFFERS from
  the provider record's own kind (`record anthropic + wire: anthropic`
  still runs the checks). REG matrix (AC1/AC2/AC3) pinned in
  `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`; AC4 IT drives a
  bifrost-shaped loopback proxy through the production anthropic adapter
  (`test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart`).
- gh-1596: the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) no longer crashes or
  corrupts input under `curl | sh` on dash (Ubuntu sh) or busybox ash
  (Alpine): `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now renders the provider/mode/
  approval menus from the live provider catalog into plain POSIX sh — the
  bashisms that killed dash (`printf -v`, `read -p`) and silently corrupted
  busybox ash are gone; the hidden API-key prompt uses `stty -echo` + a
  by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`) and the key never rides printf
  argv; EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero with no half-written
  `~/.fah`, and non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1. The wizard's temp
  config is `mktemp`-created (no predictable, symlink-followable fixed

  script under dash + busybox ash (ubuntu) and bash (macOS) on every
  `site/**` or generator change.

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a

- fix(bindings): gh-1624 — the gh-1570 binding preflight no longer kills
  translating-proxy factories. `_validateModelEndpoint`'s vendor-prefix
  verdict was fatal on ANY endpoint, so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` +

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

## Unreleased

- fix(bindings): gh-1624 — the gh-1570 binding preflight no longer kills
  translating-proxy factories. `_validateModelEndpoint`'s vendor-prefix
  verdict was fatal on ANY endpoint, so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` +
  bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exit-64'd every boot on
  1.0.576 (the prefix is a routing key on a translating proxy, not a
  dialect declaration). The vendor-prefix check is now scoped to KNOWN
  catalog endpoints — mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown

  exit 64. **Breaking-change note for 1.0.576 upgraders behind proxy
  factories: the migration is the `wire:` FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key** —

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

## Unreleased

- fix(bindings): gh-1624 — the gh-1570 binding preflight no longer kills
  translating-proxy factories. `_validateModelEndpoint`'s vendor-prefix
  verdict was fatal on ANY endpoint, so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` +
  bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exit-64'd every boot on
  1.0.576 (the prefix is a routing key on a translating proxy, not a
  dialect declaration). The vendor-prefix check is now scoped to KNOWN
  catalog endpoints — mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown
  endpoints pass" rule: real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
  api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast, unknown/private
  endpoints carry the mismatch as a `ProviderModelBinding.warnings`
  entry rendered by the boot notice (`warning: binding — …`), never
  exit 64. **Breaking-change note for 1.0.576 upgraders behind proxy
  factories: the migration is the `wire:` FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key** —
  documented now (README env-preconfig section,
  docs/agents/providers.md §Translating proxies, `--help`) with its
  caveat: the override engages only when the declared wire DIFFERS from
  the provider record's own kind (`record anthropic + wire: anthropic`
  still runs the checks). REG matrix (AC1/AC2/AC3) pinned in
  `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`; AC4 IT drives a
  bifrost-shaped loopback proxy through the production anthropic adapter
  (`test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart`).
- gh-1596: the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) no longer crashes or
  corrupts input under `curl | sh` on dash (Ubuntu sh) or busybox ash
  (Alpine): `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now renders the provider/mode/

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

  verdict was fatal on ANY endpoint, so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` +

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —

- fix(bindings): gh-1624 — the gh-1570 binding preflight no longer kills
  translating-proxy factories. `_validateModelEndpoint`'s vendor-prefix
  verdict was fatal on ANY endpoint, so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` +
  bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exit-64'd every boot on
  1.0.576 (the prefix is a routing key on a translating proxy, not a
  dialect declaration). The vendor-prefix check is now scoped to KNOWN
  catalog endpoints — mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown
  endpoints pass" rule: real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
  api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast, unknown/private
  endpoints carry the mismatch as a `ProviderModelBinding.warnings`
  entry rendered by the boot notice (`warning: binding — …`), never
  exit 64. **Breaking-change note for 1.0.576 upgraders behind proxy
  factories: the migration is the `wire:` FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key** —
  documented now (README env-preconfig section,
  docs/agents/providers.md §Translating proxies, `--help`) with its
  caveat: the override engages only when the declared wire DIFFERS from

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)
