(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

  translating-proxy factories. `_validateModelEndpoint`'s vendor-prefix
  verdict was fatal on ANY endpoint, so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` +

  factories: the migration is the `wire:` FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key** —

## Fixed — `binding.warnings` now render on all three production resolve paths

The queue lane and the flag-revalidation lane no longer swallow the binding's warnings, and the `warnings` list is pinned unmodifiable.

### Provider queue (`buildProviderQueueChain` — providers_queue_runtime.dart)

- The chain builder gained a `warnings` out-channel (same pattern as `skipped`): each chained entry's binding warnings are emitted as render-ready lines `warning: binding — <entry.label>: <warning>`.
- All three queue rebuild sites now render them:
  - boot (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — collected via a new `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)` callback and printed with the provider-queue boot notices;
  - REPL queue reload (`_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime` in agent_cli_commands.dart) — printed as they fire;
  - `/provider queue test` (`_providerQueueTest`) — printed before the probe.

### Flag revalidation (`_revalidatePartialOverride` — lib/src/cli/startup.dart)

- Now returns the effective binding's warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` carries them as a new `bindingWarnings` report field, and `bin/fah_runapp.dart` renders them on the boot's warning channel (`warning: binding — …`, stderr, next to the other restore warnings).
- Warnings the active `FA_PROVIDER_*` binding already carries are deduped — the preconfig notice renders them once; a flag that re-asserts the same binding does not double-print.

### Secondary nit

- `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` is now wrapped `List.unmodifiable` in the constructor — the "empty when every check passed / never mutated" invariant is pinned.

### Tests

- `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart`: the private-endpoint/foreign-prefix queue entry rides the chain loudly (`warnings` channel carries the entry-labelled line); a quiet entry leaves the channel empty; `ProviderQueueRuntime.build` forwards the chain's warnings to `onBindingWarning`.
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart`: `--model` over a saved private-endpoint binding surfaces the warning via `bindingWarnings`; the active-preconfig case dedupes to empty.

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —

{"content":"## Fixed — `binding.warnings` now render on all three production resolve paths

The queue lane and the flag-revalidation lane no longer swallow the binding's warnings, and the `warnings` list is pinned unmodifiable.

### Provider queue (`buildProviderQueueChain` — providers_queue_runtime.dart)

- The chain builder gained a `warnings` out-channel (same pattern as `skipped`): each chained entry's binding warnings are emitted as render-ready lines `warning: binding — <entry.label>: <warning>`.
- All three queue rebuild sites now render them:
  - boot (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — collected via a new `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)` callback and printed with the provider-queue boot notices;
  - REPL queue reload (`_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime` in agent_cli_commands.dart) — printed as they fire;
  - `/provider queue test` (`_providerQueueTest`) — printed before the probe.

### Flag revalidation (`_revalidatePartialOverride` — lib/src/cli/startup.dart)

- Now returns the effective binding's warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` carries them as a new `bindingWarnings` report field, and `bin/fah_runapp.dart` renders them on the boot's warning channel (`warning: binding — …`, stderr, next to the other restore warnings).
- Warnings the active `FA_PROVIDER_*` binding already carries are deduped — the preconfig notice renders them once; a flag that re-asserts the same binding does not double-print.

### Secondary nit

- `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` is now wrapped `List.unmodifiable` in the constructor — the "empty when every check passed / never mutated" invariant is pinned.

### Tests

## Fixed — the vendor-prefix verdict no longer fires on known ROUTER endpoints

Took option (a): the prefix verdict's fatal scope now mirrors the family branch exactly — it fires only where the endpoint carries a dialect verdict, i.e. the three family-exclusive canonical endpoints (`_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect`).

### Code (lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart)

- `_validateModelEndpoint`'s prefix branch: fatal only when `_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect(baseUrl) != null`; routers and unknown/private endpoints degrade to a `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` entry (the gh-1624 warning, wording updated to cover routers: "this endpoint carries no dialect verdict … routing key … routers and translating proxies serve several dialects from one endpoint").
- Your OpenRouter probe now resolves: `openai-completions` + record `openrouter` + `anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet` on `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` → binding with one warning, no exit 64 (`google/gemini-*` likewise).
- Family-exclusive endpoints keep the gh-1570 fail-fast in both directions (anthropic-prefixed id on the openai record's endpoint, google-prefixed id on the anthropic record's endpoint — both still throw).
- The line-366 doc claim ("unknown ids, routers and unknown endpoints pass") is true again, and the library doc + the `warnings` field dartdoc state the router-aware scope.
- Minor done too: the three copies of the catalog scan collapsed into one shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint(baseUrl)` helper — `_validateWireEndpoint`, `_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect` (now a `switch` over the matched record) and the prefix verdict all ask the same "does this endpoint carry a verdict?" lookup; `_knownCatalogEndpoint` is gone.

### Tests

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart` (gh-1624 REG group, "review" tests): the OpenRouter canonical-id probe warns on both routing families (`anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`, `google/gemini-2.0-flash`); the family-exclusive vendor endpoints stay fatal in both directions. Reproduced RED before the fix (the probe threw the exact `ConfigException` from this thread).

### Docs

- `docs/agents/providers.md`, README env-preconfig section, `--help` text, and the CHANGELOG entry now state the endpoint-carries-a-verdict scope (routers never carry one) instead of the over-broad "known catalog endpoints".

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

## Unreleased

- fix(bindings): gh-1624 — the gh-1570 binding preflight no longer kills
  translating-proxy factories. `_validateModelEndpoint`'s vendor-prefix
  verdict was fatal on ANY endpoint, so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` +
  bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exit-64'd every boot on
  1.0.576 (the prefix is a routing key on a translating proxy, not a
  dialect declaration). The vendor-prefix check is now scoped to KNOWN
  catalog endpoints — mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown
  endpoints pass" rule: real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
  api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast, unknown/private
  endpoints carry the mismatch as a `ProviderModelBinding.warnings`
  entry rendered by the boot notice (`warning: binding — …`), never
  exit 64. **Breaking-change note for 1.0.576 upgraders behind proxy
  factories: the migration is the `wire:` FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key** —
  documented now (README env-preconfig section,
  docs/agents/providers.md §Translating proxies, `--help`) with its
  caveat: the override engages only when the declared wire DIFFERS from
  the provider record's own kind (`record anthropic + wire: anthropic`
  still runs the checks). REG matrix (AC1/AC2/AC3) pinned in
  `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`; AC4 IT drives a
  bifrost-shaped loopback proxy through the production anthropic adapter

  corrupts input under `curl | sh` on dash (Ubuntu sh) or busybox ash
  (Alpine): `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now renders the provider/mode/
  approval menus from the live provider catalog into plain POSIX sh — the
  bashisms that killed dash (`printf -v`, `read -p`) and silently corrupted
  busybox ash are gone; the hidden API-key prompt uses `stty -echo` + a
  by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`) and the key never rides printf

  config is `mktemp`-created (no predictable, symlink-followable fixed

  script under dash + busybox ash (ubuntu) and bash (macOS) on every
  `site/**` or generator change.

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`

test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report

mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"content":"## Fixed — `binding.warnings` now render on all three production resolve paths

The queue lane and the flag-revalidation lane no longer swallow the binding's warnings, and the `warnings` list is pinned unmodifiable.

### Provider queue (`buildProviderQueueChain` — providers_queue_runtime.dart)

- The chain builder gained a `warnings` out-channel (same pattern as `skipped`): each chained entry's binding warnings are emitted as render-ready lines `warning: binding — <entry.label>: <warning>`.
- All three queue rebuild sites now render them:
  - boot (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — collected via a new `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)` callback and printed with the provider-queue boot notices;
  - REPL queue reload (`_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime` in agent_cli_commands.dart) — printed as they fire;
  - `/provider queue test` (`_providerQueueTest`) — printed before the probe.

### Flag revalidation (`_revalidatePartialOverride` — lib/src/cli/startup.dart)

- Now returns the effective binding's warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` carries them as a new `bindingWarnings` report field, and `bin/fah_runapp.dart` renders them on the boot's warning channel (`warning: binding — …`, stderr, next to the other restore warnings).
- Warnings the active `FA_PROVIDER_*` binding already carries are deduped — the preconfig notice renders them once; a flag that re-asserts the same binding does not double-print.

### Secondary nit

- `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` is now wrapped `List.unmodifiable` in the constructor — the "empty when every check passed / never mutated" invariant is pinned.

### Tests

- `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart`: the private-endpoint/foreign-prefix queue entry rides the chain loudly (`warnings` channel carries the entry-labelled line); a quiet entry leaves the channel empty; `ProviderQueueRuntime.build` forwards the chain's warnings to `onBindingWarning`.
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart`: `--model` over a saved private-endpoint binding surfaces the warning via `bindingWarnings`; the active-preconfig case dedupes to empty.

## Unreleased

- fix(bindings): gh-1624 — the gh-1570 binding preflight no longer kills
  translating-proxy factories. `_validateModelEndpoint`'s vendor-prefix
  verdict was fatal on ANY endpoint, so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` +
  bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exit-64'd every boot on
  1.0.576 (the prefix is a routing key on a translating proxy, not a
  dialect declaration). The vendor-prefix check is now scoped to KNOWN
  catalog endpoints — mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown

## Unreleased

  verdict was fatal on ANY endpoint, so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` +

  1.0.576 (the prefix is a routing key on a translating proxy, not a
  dialect declaration). The vendor-prefix check is now scoped to KNOWN
  catalog endpoints — mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown
  endpoints pass" rule: real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
  api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast, unknown/private
  endpoints carry the mismatch as a `ProviderModelBinding.warnings`
  entry rendered by the boot notice (`warning: binding — …`), never
  exit 64. **Breaking-change note for 1.0.576 upgraders behind proxy
  factories: the migration is the `wire:` FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key** —
  documented now (README env-preconfig section,
  docs/agents/providers.md §Translating proxies, `--help`) with its
  caveat: the override engages only when the declared wire DIFFERS from

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving

  catalog endpoints — mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown
  endpoints pass" rule: real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
  api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast, unknown/private
  endpoints carry the mismatch as a `ProviderModelBinding.warnings`
  entry rendered by the boot notice (`warning: binding — …`), never
  exit 64. **Breaking-change note for 1.0.576 upgraders behind proxy
  factories: the migration is the `wire:` FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key** —
  documented now (README env-preconfig section,

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report

{"newText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). Both dialect verdicts fire ONLY on the
three family-exclusive vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
api.openai.com, generativelanguage) — the vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) alike; that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. ROUTERS (OpenRouter, Copilot, DIAL, kimi) never
carry a verdict — they serve many families and route `vendor/` prefixes
as keys (OpenRouter's canonical ids ARE `anthropic/claude-*`), so a
`claude-*` id on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes
the family check and a foreign prefix boots with a warning. On
unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/` prefix is likewise treated as a
routing key, not a dialect declaration: a mismatch boots with a
`warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64. Translating proxies
(bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving several dialect paths such
as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra configuration since gh-1624.
The warning is rendered wherever the binding boots: the `FA_PROVIDER_*`
notice, the provider queue (per entry, at boot and `/provider queue
test`), and the `--model`/`--base-url` flag revalidation.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks
still run. The override silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller
asserts the endpoint speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report
(`wire override:`) so a silenced check is never invisible.","oldText":"## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key; `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`
takes it as `wire:`) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks,
overriding the provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages
ONLY when the declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind —
`record anthropic + wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks

# gh-1624 rework — review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- ⚠️ **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqplU`** — `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` were rendered only on the `FA_PROVIDER_*` boot notice; the provider-queue chain and the `--model`/`--base-url` revalidation dropped them (silent riders). **Fixed.**
- ⚠️ **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqpo9`** — the "known endpoint" scoping kept the vendor-prefix verdict fatal on known ROUTER endpoints (OpenRouter's canonical ids are `anthropic/claude-*`/`google/gemini-*` → still exit 64), contradicting the doc claim "routers … pass". **Fixed via option (a).**
- 💡 **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqptD`** — `docs/agents/providers.md` over-broadened the family verdict's scope (it fires only on the three family-exclusive endpoints, never on routers). **Fixed.**
- The remaining 3 open conversations in `pr_discussions_raw.json` carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` and are machine notices (review-verdict record, rework-consume audit, and the APPROVE summary comment) — not reply targets, nothing to fix in code.
- CI was green at rework start; no merge conflicts.

## Approach

- **Warnings on every resolve path (thread 1).** `buildProviderQueueChain` gained a `warnings` out-channel (the `skipped` pattern) emitting render-ready `warning: binding — <entry>: <note>` lines; all three queue rebuild sites render them — boot (`ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)` → the provider-queue boot notices in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`), REPL queue reload (`_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime`), and `/provider queue test`. `_revalidatePartialOverride` now returns the effective binding's warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` carries them as a new `bindingWarnings` report field and the boot prints them (`warning: binding — …`, next to the other restore warnings). Warnings the active `FA_PROVIDER_*` binding already carries are deduped so the preconfig notice never double-prints. Secondary nit done: `warnings` is pinned `List.unmodifiable`.
- **Router endpoints (thread 2, option a).** The prefix verdict's fatal scope now mirrors the family branch exactly: fatal only when the endpoint carries a dialect verdict (`_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect(baseUrl) != null` — the three family-exclusive canonical endpoints); routers and unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a warning ("this endpoint carries no dialect verdict … routing key"). gh-1570 fail-fast is preserved on the vendor endpoints in both directions. The minor is done too: the three catalog-scan copies collapsed into one shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint(baseUrl)` helper (`_validateWireEndpoint`, `_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect`, the prefix verdict); `_knownCatalogEndpoint` removed. The line-366 doc claim ("unknown ids, routers and unknown endpoints pass") is true again.
- **Docs (thread 3).** `docs/agents/providers.md` states the exact scope (both verdicts fire only on api.anthropic.com / api.openai.com / generativelanguage; routers never carry a verdict — `claude-*` on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes) and names where the warning renders; README, `--help` text and the CHANGELOG entry updated to the same scope.
- TDD throughout: each thread reproduced by a failing test first (the OpenRouter probe reproduced the thread's exact `ConfigException`), then the minimum fix turned it green.

## Files Modified

## Unreleased

- fix(bindings): gh-1624 — the gh-1570 binding preflight no longer kills
  translating-proxy factories. `_validateModelEndpoint`'s vendor-prefix
  verdict was fatal on ANY endpoint, so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` +
  bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exit-64'd every boot on
  1.0.576 (the prefix is a routing key on a translating proxy, not a
  dialect declaration). The vendor-prefix check is now scoped to KNOWN
  catalog endpoints — mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown
  endpoints pass" rule: real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com,
  api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast, unknown/private
  endpoints carry the mismatch as a `ProviderModelBinding.warnings`
  entry rendered by the boot notice (`warning: binding — …`), never
  exit 64. **Breaking-change note for 1.0.576 upgraders behind proxy
  factories: the migration is the `wire:` FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key** —
  documented now (README env-preconfig section,
  docs/agents/providers.md §Translating proxies, `--help`) with its
  caveat: the override engages only when the declared wire DIFFERS from
  the provider record's own kind (`record anthropic + wire: anthropic`
  still runs the checks). REG matrix (AC1/AC2/AC3) pinned in
  `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`; AC4 IT drives a
  bifrost-shaped loopback proxy through the production anthropic adapter
  (`test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart`).
- gh-1596: the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) no longer crashes or
  corrupts input under `curl | sh` on dash (Ubuntu sh) or busybox ash
  (Alpine): `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now renders the provider/mode/
  approval menus from the live provider catalog into plain POSIX sh — the
  bashisms that killed dash (`printf -v`, `read -p`) and silently corrupted
  busybox ash are gone; the hidden API-key prompt uses `stty -echo` + a
  by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`) and the key never rides printf
  argv; EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero with no half-written
  `~/.fah`, and non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1. The wizard's temp
  config is `mktemp`-created (no predictable, symlink-followable fixed
  path). A new path-triggered `installer-portability` CI leg proves the
  script under dash + busybox ash (ubuntu) and bash (macOS) on every
  `site/**` or generator change.
- fix(cli): gh-1572 — `fa` boot no longer rewrites `~/.fah/config.yaml`

  fresh `CliConfig` carrying only some fields and `persistConfig()` ran

{"content":"# gh-1624 rework — review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- ⚠️ **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqplU`** — `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` were rendered only on the `FA_PROVIDER_*` boot notice; the provider-queue chain and the `--model`/`--base-url` revalidation dropped them (silent riders). **Fixed.**
- ⚠️ **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqpo9`** — the "known endpoint" scoping kept the vendor-prefix verdict fatal on known ROUTER endpoints (OpenRouter's canonical ids are `anthropic/claude-*`/`google/gemini-*` → still exit 64), contradicting the doc claim "routers … pass". **Fixed via option (a).**
- 💡 **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqptD`** — `docs/agents/providers.md` over-broadened the family verdict's scope (it fires only on the three family-exclusive endpoints, never on routers). **Fixed.**
- The remaining 3 open conversations in `pr_discussions_raw.json` carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` and are machine notices (review-verdict record, rework-consume audit, and the APPROVE summary comment) — not reply targets, nothing to fix in code.
- CI was green at rework start; no merge conflicts.

## Approach

- **Warnings on every resolve path (thread 1).** `buildProviderQueueChain` gained a `warnings` out-channel (the `skipped` pattern) emitting render-ready `warning: binding — <entry>: <note>` lines; all three queue rebuild sites render them — boot (`ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)` → the provider-queue boot notices in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`), REPL queue reload (`_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime`), and `/provider queue test`. `_revalidatePartialOverride` now returns the effective binding's warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` carries them as a new `bindingWarnings` report field and the boot prints them (`warning: binding — …`, next to the other restore warnings). Warnings the active `FA_PROVIDER_*` binding already carries are deduped so the preconfig notice never double-prints. Secondary nit done: `warnings` is pinned `List.unmodifiable`.
- **Router endpoints (thread 2, option a).** The prefix verdict's fatal scope now mirrors the family branch exactly: fatal only when the endpoint carries a dialect verdict (`_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect(baseUrl) != null` — the three family-exclusive canonical endpoints); routers and unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a warning ("this endpoint carries no dialect verdict … routing key"). gh-1570 fail-fast is preserved on the vendor endpoints in both directions. The minor is done too: the three catalog-scan copies collapsed into one shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint(baseUrl)` helper (`_validateWireEndpoint`, `_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect`, the prefix verdict); `_knownCatalogEndpoint` removed. The line-366 doc claim ("unknown ids, routers and unknown endpoints pass") is true again.
- **Docs (thread 3).** `docs/agents/providers.md` states the exact scope (both verdicts fire only on api.anthropic.com / api.openai.com / generativelanguage; routers never carry a verdict — `claude-*` on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes) and names where the warning renders; README, `--help` text and the CHANGELOG entry updated to the same scope.
- TDD throughout: each thread reproduced by a failing test first (the OpenRouter probe reproduced the thread's exact `ConfigException`), then the minimum fix turned it green.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart` — router-aware verdict scoping, shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint`, unmodifiable `warnings`, dartdocs.
- `lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue_runtime.dart` — `buildProviderQueueChain(warnings:)` out-channel; `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)`.
- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — `_revalidatePartialOverride` returns (deduped) binding warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` record gains `bindingWarnings`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart` — queue reload + `/provider queue test` render the warnings.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot renders queue binding warnings and the flag-path `bindingWarnings`.
- `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart`, `README.md`, `docs/agents/providers.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — scope-accurate docs.

## Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart` — new "review" tests in the gh-1624 REG group: OpenRouter canonical-id probe (`anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`, `google/gemini-2.0-flash`) resolves with a routing-key warning instead of exit 64; family-exclusive vendor endpoints stay fatal in both directions; `warnings` rejects mutation (`throwsUnsupportedError`).
- `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart` — the private-endpoint/foreign-prefix queue entry chains loudly (entry-labelled warning line); a quiet entry leaves the channel empty; `ProviderQueueRuntime.build` forwards warnings to `onBindingWarning`.
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — `--model` over a saved private-endpoint binding surfaces the warning via `bindingWarnings`; the active-preconfig duplicate is suppressed.
- Touched suites green after the fix: binding + queue + startup + env-preconfig + the bifrost loopback IT (230 passed). Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`) run recorded in the rework validation.

{"content":"# gh-1624 rework — review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- ⚠️ **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqplU`** — `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` were rendered only on the `FA_PROVIDER_*` boot notice; the provider-queue chain and the `--model`/`--base-url` revalidation dropped them (silent riders). **Fixed.**
- ⚠️ **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqpo9`** — the "known endpoint" scoping kept the vendor-prefix verdict fatal on known ROUTER endpoints (OpenRouter's canonical ids are `anthropic/claude-*`/`google/gemini-*` → still exit 64), contradicting the doc claim "routers … pass". **Fixed via option (a).**
- 💡 **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqptD`** — `docs/agents/providers.md` over-broadened the family verdict's scope (it fires only on the three family-exclusive endpoints, never on routers). **Fixed.**
- The remaining 3 open conversations in `pr_discussions_raw.json` carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` and are machine notices (review-verdict record, rework-consume audit, and the APPROVE summary comment) — not reply targets, nothing to fix in code.
- CI was green at rework start; no merge conflicts.

## Approach

- **Warnings on every resolve path (thread 1).** `buildProviderQueueChain` gained a `warnings` out-channel (the `skipped` pattern) emitting render-ready `warning: binding — <entry>: <note>` lines; all three queue rebuild sites render them — boot (`ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)` → the provider-queue boot notices in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`), REPL queue reload (`_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime`), and `/provider queue test`. `_revalidatePartialOverride` now returns the effective binding's warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` carries them as a new `bindingWarnings` report field and the boot prints them (`warning: binding — …`, next to the other restore warnings). Warnings the active `FA_PROVIDER_*` binding already carries are deduped so the preconfig notice never double-prints. Secondary nit done: `warnings` is pinned `List.unmodifiable`.
- **Router endpoints (thread 2, option a).** The prefix verdict's fatal scope now mirrors the family branch exactly: fatal only when the endpoint carries a dialect verdict (`_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect(baseUrl) != null` — the three family-exclusive canonical endpoints); routers and unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a warning ("this endpoint carries no dialect verdict … routing key"). gh-1570 fail-fast is preserved on the vendor endpoints in both directions. The minor is done too: the three catalog-scan copies collapsed into one shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint(baseUrl)` helper (`_validateWireEndpoint`, `_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect`, the prefix verdict); `_knownCatalogEndpoint` removed. The line-366 doc claim ("unknown ids, routers and unknown endpoints pass") is true again.
- **Docs (thread 3).** `docs/agents/providers.md` states the exact scope (both verdicts fire only on api.anthropic.com / api.openai.com / generativelanguage; routers never carry a verdict — `claude-*` on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes) and names where the warning renders; README, `--help` text and the CHANGELOG entry updated to the same scope.
- TDD throughout: each thread reproduced by a failing test first (the OpenRouter probe reproduced the thread's exact `ConfigException`), then the minimum fix turned it green.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart` — router-aware verdict scoping, shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint`, unmodifiable `warnings`, dartdocs.
- `lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue_runtime.dart` — `buildProviderQueueChain(warnings:)` out-channel; `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)`.
- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — `_revalidatePartialOverride` returns (deduped) binding warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` record gains `bindingWarnings`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart` — queue reload + `/provider queue test` render the warnings.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot renders queue binding warnings and the flag-path `bindingWarnings`.
- `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart`, `README.md`, `docs/agents/providers.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — scope-accurate docs.

## Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart` — new "review" tests in the gh-1624 REG group: OpenRouter canonical-id probe (`anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`, `google/gemini-2.0-flash`) resolves with a routing-key warning instead of exit 64; family-exclusive vendor endpoints stay fatal in both directions; `warnings` rejects mutation (`throwsUnsupportedError`).
- `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart` — the private-endpoint/foreign-prefix queue entry chains loudly (entry-labelled warning line); a quiet entry leaves the channel empty; `ProviderQueueRuntime.build` forwards warnings to `onBindingWarning`.
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — `--model` over a saved private-endpoint binding surfaces the warning via `bindingWarnings`; the active-preconfig duplicate is suppressed.
- Touched suites green after the fix: binding + queue + startup + env-preconfig + the bifrost loopback IT (230 passed). Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`) run recorded in the rework validation.

{"content":"# gh-1624 rework — review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- ⚠️ **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqplU`** — `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` were rendered only on the `FA_PROVIDER_*` boot notice; the provider-queue chain and the `--model`/`--base-url` revalidation dropped them (silent riders). **Fixed.**
- ⚠️ **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqpo9`** — the "known endpoint" scoping kept the vendor-prefix verdict fatal on known ROUTER endpoints (OpenRouter's canonical ids are `anthropic/claude-*`/`google/gemini-*` → still exit 64), contradicting the doc claim "routers … pass". **Fixed via option (a).**
- 💡 **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqptD`** — `docs/agents/providers.md` over-broadened the family verdict's scope (it fires only on the three family-exclusive endpoints, never on routers). **Fixed.**
- The remaining 3 open conversations in `pr_discussions_raw.json` carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` and are machine notices (review-verdict record, rework-consume audit, and the APPROVE summary comment) — not reply targets, nothing to fix in code.
- CI was green at rework start; no merge conflicts.

## Approach

- **Warnings on every resolve path (thread 1).** `buildProviderQueueChain` gained a `warnings` out-channel (the `skipped` pattern) emitting render-ready `warning: binding — <entry>: <note>` lines; all three queue rebuild sites render them — boot (`ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)` → the provider-queue boot notices in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`), REPL queue reload (`_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime`), and `/provider queue test`. `_revalidatePartialOverride` now returns the effective binding's warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` carries them as a new `bindingWarnings` report field and the boot prints them (`warning: binding — …`, next to the other restore warnings). Warnings the active `FA_PROVIDER_*` binding already carries are deduped so the preconfig notice never double-prints. Secondary nit done: `warnings` is pinned `List.unmodifiable`.
- **Router endpoints (thread 2, option a).** The prefix verdict's fatal scope now mirrors the family branch exactly: fatal only when the endpoint carries a dialect verdict (`_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect(baseUrl) != null` — the three family-exclusive canonical endpoints); routers and unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a warning ("this endpoint carries no dialect verdict … routing key"). gh-1570 fail-fast is preserved on the vendor endpoints in both directions. The minor is done too: the three catalog-scan copies collapsed into one shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint(baseUrl)` helper (`_validateWireEndpoint`, `_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect`, the prefix verdict); `_knownCatalogEndpoint` removed. The line-366 doc claim ("unknown ids, routers and unknown endpoints pass") is true again.
- **Docs (thread 3).** `docs/agents/providers.md` states the exact scope (both verdicts fire only on api.anthropic.com / api.openai.com / generativelanguage; routers never carry a verdict — `claude-*` on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes) and names where the warning renders; README, `--help` text and the CHANGELOG entry updated to the same scope.
- TDD throughout: each thread reproduced by a failing test first (the OpenRouter probe reproduced the thread's exact `ConfigException`), then the minimum fix turned it green.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart` — router-aware verdict scoping, shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint`, unmodifiable `warnings`, dartdocs.
- `lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue_runtime.dart` — `buildProviderQueueChain(warnings:)` out-channel; `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)`.
- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — `_revalidatePartialOverride` returns (deduped) binding warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` record gains `bindingWarnings`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart` — queue reload + `/provider queue test` render the warnings.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot renders queue binding warnings and the flag-path `bindingWarnings`.
- `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart`, `README.md`, `docs/agents/providers.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — scope-accurate docs.

## Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart` — new "review" tests in the gh-1624 REG group: OpenRouter canonical-id probe (`anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`, `google/gemini-2.0-flash`) resolves with a routing-key warning instead of exit 64; family-exclusive vendor endpoints stay fatal in both directions; `warnings` rejects mutation (`throwsUnsupportedError`).
- `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart` — the private-endpoint/foreign-prefix queue entry chains loudly (entry-labelled warning line); a quiet entry leaves the channel empty; `ProviderQueueRuntime.build` forwards warnings to `onBindingWarning`.
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — `--model` over a saved private-endpoint binding surfaces the warning via `bindingWarnings`; the active-preconfig duplicate is suppressed.
- Touched suites green after the fix: binding + queue + startup + env-preconfig + the bifrost loopback IT (230 passed). Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`) run recorded in the rework validation.

- 💡 **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqptD`** — `docs/agents/providers.md` over-broadened the family verdict's scope (it fires only on the three family-exclusive endpoints, never on routers). **Fixed.**

- **Warnings on every resolve path (thread 1).** `buildProviderQueueChain` gained a `warnings` out-channel (the `skipped` pattern) emitting render-ready `warning: binding — <entry>: <note>` lines; all three queue rebuild sites render them — boot (`ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)` → the provider-queue boot notices in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`), REPL queue reload (`_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime`), and `/provider queue test`. `_revalidatePartialOverride` now returns the effective binding's warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` carries them as a new `bindingWarnings` report field and the boot prints them (`warning: binding — …`, next to the other restore warnings). Warnings the active `FA_PROVIDER_*` binding already carries are deduped so the preconfig notice never double-prints. Secondary nit done: `warnings` is pinned `List.unmodifiable`.
- **Router endpoints (thread 2, option a).** The prefix verdict's fatal scope now mirrors the family branch exactly: fatal only when the endpoint carries a dialect verdict (`_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect(baseUrl) != null` — the three family-exclusive canonical endpoints); routers and unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a warning ("this endpoint carries no dialect verdict … routing key"). gh-1570 fail-fast is preserved on the vendor endpoints in both directions. {"content":"# gh-1624 rework — review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- ⚠️ **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqplU`** — `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` were rendered only on the `FA_PROVIDER_*` boot notice; the provider-queue chain and the `--model`/`--base-url` revalidation dropped them (silent riders). **Fixed.**
- ⚠️ **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqpo9`** — the "known endpoint" scoping kept the vendor-prefix verdict fatal on known ROUTER endpoints (OpenRouter's canonical ids are `anthropic/claude-*`/`google/gemini-*` → still exit 64), contradicting the doc claim "routers … pass". **Fixed via option (a).**
- 💡 **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqptD`** — `docs/agents/providers.md` over-broadened the family verdict's scope (it fires only on the three family-exclusive endpoints, never on routers). **Fixed.**
- The remaining 3 open conversations in `pr_discussions_raw.json` carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` and are machine notices (review-verdict record, rework-consume audit, and the APPROVE summary comment) — not reply targets, nothing to fix in code.
- CI was green at rework start; no merge conflicts.

## Approach

- **Warnings on every resolve path (thread 1).** `buildProviderQueueChain` gained a `warnings` out-channel (the `skipped` pattern) emitting render-ready `warning: binding — <entry>: <note>` lines; all three queue rebuild sites render them — boot (`ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)` → the provider-queue boot notices in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`), REPL queue reload (`_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime`), and `/provider queue test`. `_revalidatePartialOverride` now returns the effective binding's warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` carries them as a new `bindingWarnings` report field and the boot prints them (`warning: binding — …`, next to the other restore warnings). Warnings the active `FA_PROVIDER_*` binding already carries are deduped so the preconfig notice never double-prints. Secondary nit done: `warnings` is pinned `List.unmodifiable`.
- **Router endpoints (thread 2, option a).** The prefix verdict's fatal scope now mirrors the family branch exactly: fatal only when the endpoint carries a dialect verdict (`_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect(baseUrl) != null` — the three family-exclusive canonical endpoints); routers and unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a warning ("this endpoint carries no dialect verdict … routing key"). gh-1570 fail-fast is preserved on the vendor endpoints in both directions. The minor is done too: the three catalog-scan copies collapsed into one shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint(baseUrl)` helper (`_validateWireEndpoint`, `_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect`, the prefix verdict); `_knownCatalogEndpoint` removed. The line-366 doc claim ("unknown ids, routers and unknown endpoints pass") is true again.
- **Docs (thread 3).** `docs/agents/providers.md` states the exact scope (both verdicts fire only on api.anthropic.com / api.openai.com / generativelanguage; routers never carry a verdict — `claude-*` on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes) and names where the warning renders; README, `--help` text and the CHANGELOG entry updated to the same scope.
- TDD throughout: each thread reproduced by a failing test first (the OpenRouter probe reproduced the thread's exact `ConfigException`), then the minimum fix turned it green.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart` — router-aware verdict scoping, shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint`, unmodifiable `warnings`, dartdocs.
- `lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue_runtime.dart` — `buildProviderQueueChain(warnings:)` out-channel; `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)`.
- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — `_revalidatePartialOverride` returns (deduped) binding warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` record gains `bindingWarnings`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart` — queue reload + `/provider queue test` render the warnings.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot renders queue binding warnings and the flag-path `bindingWarnings`.
- `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart`, `README.md`, `docs/agents/providers.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — scope-accurate docs.

## Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart` — new "review" tests in the gh-1624 REG group: OpenRouter canonical-id probe (`anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`, `google/gemini-2.0-flash`) resolves with a routing-key warning instead of exit 64; family-exclusive vendor endpoints stay fatal in both directions; `warnings` rejects mutation (`throwsUnsupportedError`).
- `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart` — the private-endpoint/foreign-prefix queue entry chains loudly (entry-labelled warning line); a quiet entry leaves the channel empty; `ProviderQueueRuntime.build` forwards warnings to `onBindingWarning`.
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — `--model` over a saved private-endpoint binding surfaces the warning via `bindingWarnings`; the active-preconfig duplicate is suppressed.
- Touched suites green after the fix: binding + queue + startup + env-preconfig + the bifrost loopback IT (230 passed). Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`) run recorded in the rework validation.

{"content":"# gh-1624 rework — review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- ⚠️ **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqplU`** — `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` were rendered only on the `FA_PROVIDER_*` boot notice; the provider-queue chain and the `--model`/`--base-url` revalidation dropped them (silent riders). **Fixed.**

- 💡 **Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sqptD`** — `docs/agents/providers.md` over-broadened the family verdict's scope (it fires only on the three family-exclusive endpoints, never on routers). **Fixed.**

- CI was green at rework start; no merge conflicts.

## Approach

- **Warnings on every resolve path (thread 1).** `buildProviderQueueChain` gained a `warnings` out-channel (the `skipped` pattern) emitting render-ready `warning: binding — <entry>: <note>` lines; all three queue rebuild sites render them — boot (`ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)` → the provider-queue boot notices in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`), REPL queue reload (`_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime`), and `/provider queue test`. `_revalidatePartialOverride` now returns the effective binding's warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` carries them as a new `bindingWarnings` report field and the boot prints them (`warning: binding — …`, next to the other restore warnings). Warnings the active `FA_PROVIDER_*` binding already carries are deduped so the preconfig notice never double-prints. Secondary nit done: `warnings` is pinned `List.unmodifiable`.
- **Router endpoints (thread 2, option a).** The prefix verdict's fatal scope now mirrors the family branch exactly: fatal only when the endpoint carries a dialect verdict (`_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect(baseUrl) != null` — the three family-exclusive canonical endpoints); routers and unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a warning ("this endpoint carries no dialect verdict … routing key"). gh-1570 fail-fast is preserved on the vendor endpoints in both directions. The minor is done too: the three catalog-scan copies collapsed into one shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint(baseUrl)` helper (`_validateWireEndpoint`, `_familyExclusiveEndpointDialect`, the prefix verdict); `_knownCatalogEndpoint` removed. The line-366 doc claim ("unknown ids, routers and unknown endpoints pass") is true again.
- **Docs (thread 3).** `docs/agents/providers.md` states the exact scope (both verdicts fire only on api.anthropic.com / api.openai.com / generativelanguage; routers never carry a verdict — `claude-*` on an openai-completions binding over OpenRouter passes) and names where the warning renders; README, `--help` text and the CHANGELOG entry updated to the same scope.
- TDD throughout: each thread reproduced by a failing test first (the OpenRouter probe reproduced the thread's exact `ConfigException`), then the minimum fix turned it green.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart` — router-aware verdict scoping, shared `_matchingCatalogEndpoint`, unmodifiable `warnings`, dartdocs.
- `lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue_runtime.dart` — `buildProviderQueueChain(warnings:)` out-channel; `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(onBindingWarning:)`.
- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — `_revalidatePartialOverride` returns (deduped) binding warnings; `resolveEffectiveCliArgs` record gains `bindingWarnings`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart` — queue reload + `/provider queue test` render the warnings.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot renders queue binding warnings and the flag-path `bindingWarnings`.
- `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart`, `README.md`, `docs/agents/providers.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — scope-accurate docs.
